I've been farming this little plot for 20 years now. I'm in my mid-forties, finished primary school, and everything I know comes from my own fields and watching the neighbors. With only 1.8 mu and five people at home — my husband, my mother-in-law, and two children — every yuan matters. I split the land: about 1 mu goes to wheat then maize for grain, and the other 0.8 mu stays in cotton for cash. The wheat we mostly eat, the maize we sell or feed the chickens, and the cotton pays for school fees.

For the wheat, I'll plant in early October, same as Lao Wang next door. I saved some seed from last year but bought a little to refresh — about 15 yuan for the mu. I'll spread about half a bag of compound fertilizer before planting, maybe 25 kg, and if the wheat looks yellow at jointing come March, I'll topdress some urea. I don't want to put too much — fertilizer got expensive last year — but I also don't want to lose yield. Better to waste a little money than to go hungry. I'll irrigate twice: once before winter freeze and once at jointing. Pumping water from the well costs about 30 yuan each time, so I won't do more unless it's very dry. We do all the work ourselves — my husband, my mother-in-law, and me. No hired labor. We can't afford it. If the weather is normal, I expect about 350 kg per mu.

Maize is rushed. We harvest the wheat in early June and plant the maize right away, sometimes within two or three days. The window is tight. I'll buy hybrid seed — can't save that — about 45 yuan per mu. I'll put down some compound fertilizer in the row at planting, around 10 kg of nitrogen worth. If it rains well, maybe I don't irrigate, but usually I give it one watering when it's tasseling. I expect about 400 kg per mu if the weather holds.

The cotton needs more care. I plant in late April. It always gets bollworms, so I have to spray insecticide at least twice. I'll put fertilizer down at planting and again at flowering — about 10 kg nitrogen per mu total. Irrigate twice. Picking takes forever, even on 0.8 mu. My daughter helps in autumn when school lets out, and my mother-in-law picks too. I hope for about 220 kg of lint per mu.

All together, inputs will cost me around 650 yuan. That's a lot for us. I'd like to keep a little cash in my pocket for emergencies — if someone gets sick, we need money right away. But if I don't spend on seed and fertilizer, I'll lose more than I save. So I'll pay what I have to, and hope this year is kind.
